messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Metering anomaly detected: rapid token-count delta vs baseline for customer cohort 'playground-*' (window 2026-03-14T22:00Z - 2026-03-14T22:30Z). Auto-overage flags raised. Paging oncall.

ina (oncall): I got paged for the metering alert. Looking at the dashboard now — token ingestion spike + downstream reporter backlog. tagging @tom, @derek. Any quick eyes on Kafka/consumer groups?

tom (eng-infra): seeing a consumer restart on metering-reporter-3 at ~22:04Z. Consumer group shows reprocessing of ~1.2M messages. offsets jumped backwards. Possible duplicate emit to billing DB. Pulling consumer logs.

maria (sre): noted. Do we know if this was a manual deploy or crashloop? I can tail the pod logs if you already have the pod name.

tom (eng-infra): pod metering-reporter-3-7f8c9 crashed and restarted after OOM. OOM reason: peak memory from KV cache + large batch. Crash loop ended once restarted by k8s. consumer committed, then reprocessed when it came up — looks like we double-inserted partial uploads.

maria (sre): log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T22:03:58Z INFO aggregator: received batch id=ab12 size=45000 tokens
2026-03-14T22:04:01Z ERROR reporter: failed to flush to clickhouse: write timeout
2026-03-14T22:04:02Z INFO reporter: restarting consumer group metering-reporter-3
2026-03-14T22:04:07Z INFO reporter: reprocessing from offset 154321000 (committed offset 154320000)
2026-03-14T22:04:12Z WARN reporter: duplicate detection missed for batch ab12
```

ina (oncall): that duplicate detection warns me — so duplicates likely went through into the billing aggregates. Derek, do we have customers already getting overage emails or enforcement? billing-bot, any flags?

billing-bot: ALERT: 32 accounts moved into OVERAGE status between 22:05Z-22:10Z. Estimated additional billed tokens: ~3.8M. Overage emails queued: 28.

derek (billing): OK — we should pause enforcement immediately (no automatic charging / API rate-limits tied to overage) and cancel queued emails. We can do credits after we confirm actual counts. Is it safe to pause the enforcement? What workflow?

maria (sre): I recommend three steps now: 1) Pause reporter reprocess job to stop further duplicates, 2) Freeze overage enforcement and cancel outgoing emails, 3) Run an on-the-fly de-dupe query to estimate duplicates and compute provisional adjustments.

tom (eng-infra): executing step 1 now: `kubectl scale deployment metering-reporter --replicas=0 -n prod` -> scaling to 0. Confirmed: no reporter pods running.

derek (billing): executing step 2: calling billing controlplane: `POST /admin/overage/state/pause` body `{window_start: "2026-03-14T22:00Z", window_end: "2026-03-14T22:30Z", reason: "ingestion duplication due to consumer restart"}`. Response: `200 OK` — overage enforcement paused and queued emails cancelled.

ina (oncall): thanks. Maria, can you run the de-dupe estimate? If we can get a safe delta number we can inform ops and customer success.

maria (sre): running ad-hoc query against the metering-aggregates table to compare unique request ids vs counted tokens. Query (simplified):
```
SELECT window_start, sum(tokens) as raw_tokens, sum(distinct request_id_tokens) as unique_tokens
FROM metering_aggregates
WHERE window_start >= '2026-03-14 22:00:00'
GROUP BY window_start;
```
Prelim results: raw_tokens = 18,920,432 ; unique_tokens = 15,121,987 -> delta ~3.8M tokens (matches billing-bot estimate).

derek (billing): That aligns. Action: we'll grant provisional credits for the delta and notify affected customers with an explanatory note. I'll draft a short message for CS to send after engineering approves final numbers.

ina (oncall): Are there any other replay/backfill processes that could reintroduce duplicates? We need to lock down consumer commits and ensure idempotency.

tom (eng-infra): Good catch. The re-ingest pipeline had a reprocessor job kicked from the alerting runbook earlier this week for a historical backfill — it seems the reprocessor picked the same offset range due to an off-by-one in its commit logic. I'll open a patch to make commit idempotent and add stronger preconditions to the backfill tool.

maria (sre): For immediate mitigation, I started a safe de-dupe job that will create a reconciliation table and mark suspected duplicate batches so billing can ignore them for final invoicing. Running now; ETA ~15-25m.

incident-bot: Update posted to status page draft: "Investigating metering anomaly affecting token counts and overage flags. We've paused enforcement and are running reconciliation. No customer charges will be applied for the affected window while we investigate." (will not be published until derek approves)

derek (billing): Approve posting. Also pinging CS to hold outbound emails: `@cs-team please hold any automated overage notices for accounts flagged in the 22:00Z window; we'll send a consolidated update once reconciled.`

ina (oncall): Handing off monitoring to maria for the next 6h. I'll remain reachable for escalation. Maria, please confirm when reconciliation completes and whether any further manual adjustments are required.

maria (sre): Reconciliation complete: duplicates identified and tagged. Summary: approx 3,793,445 tokens attributable to duplicate ingestion from batches ab12..ab36. Created reconciliation table `metering_reconciles.2026_03_14_2200` and flagged 32 accounts.

maria (sre): Proposed next steps: 1) run safe rollback to subtract duplicate tokens from customer's usage snapshot (non-destructive; keep audit trail), 2) resume reporter only after patch deployed to prevent reoccurrence, 3) postmortem and customer outreach.

tom (eng-infra): Patch PR opened: `fix(reporter): idempotent commit + backfill-safety-check` -> will deploy to canary first. Commands to deploy canary: `kubectl set image deployment/metering-reporter metering-reporter=registry/redwood/metering-reporter:fix-idempotent-canary -n prod`.

derek (billing): I'll prepare credit adjustments and coordinate the CS message. Draft message: "We detected a metering issue that resulted in duplicate token counts between 22:00-22:30 UTC on 2026-03-14. We've paused enforcement, issued credits where appropriate, and will follow up with details and a postmortem."

maria (sre): executing rollback adjustment: `UPDATE customer_usage SET tokens = tokens - reconciled_duplicates WHERE reconcile_id = '2026_03_14_2200'` (wrapped by transactional migration script). Script ran and returned: `applied to 32 accounts; total tokens adjusted = 3,793,445`.

billing-bot: Billing ledger entries queued for credits: 32 customers; total credit tokens: 3,793,445.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> enforcement paused, duplicate tokens removed, reporter scaled to 0. Next action: deploy fix and reopen reporter in canary.

tom (eng-infra): deploying canary now. Monitor logs for duplicate detection.

maria (sre): canary logs look clean for 10m so far. No duplicate-warning entries.

derek (billing): CS message sent as planned. Finance notified for credit ledger.

ina (oncall): handing incident to maria for overnight watch. Please include follow-up postmortem with timeline, root cause (OOM -> consumer restart -> reprocess + backfill off-by-one commit), and action items (hard limits on batch size, memory safeties, backfill gating, stronger uniqueness checks).

maria (sre): will author postmortem and link action items to eng backlog. Preliminary RCA: 1) unbounded batch memory -> OOM, 2) restart triggered reprocessing without strict idempotency, 3) backfill/replay allowed overlapping offsets due to off-by-one commit logic.

nina (oncall): thanks all. Closing pager and marking as mitigated. Final reminder: schedule a billing reconciliation review with Finance and CS tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
